Case overview

A four-year redesign, measured

Sydney Gentle Care is a self-sourced NDIS provider client I've worked with continuously since 2022, taking their site from a dense, dated 2022 build to an accessible, high-performing one, and staying on as their design contact for every update since.

Role
UX/UI Designer, 2022–2026
Self-sourced client, sole designer throughout.
Sector
NDIS / disability support
Accessibility wasn't optional, it was the brief.
Recognition
2026 Enablement Award
Most Compassionate Care Provider, NDIS/disability sector.
The brief

From a 13-service, multi-page site to one clear path

The original 2022 site buried around thirteen services across a dense, multi-page structure with no clear entry point for someone trying to work out if they were even eligible for support. The redesign replaced that with a one-page layout, intuitive top navigation, every service organized with a short plain-language explanation, a dedicated NDIS support and plan-management section, and a clear eligibility-check entry point.

Services are grouped into filterable categories rather than a flat list of thirteen, and NDIS Support Coordination and Plan Management sit side by side so a visitor can compare them in one glance instead of hunting across pages.

Accessibility audit

Designing for the people actually using it

Given the audience, accessibility wasn't a checklist item added at the end, it shaped structure, contrast, and navigation from the first pass, aligned with NDIS Practice Standards framing rather than generic WCAG box-ticking.

The FAQ follows the same logic as the rest of the redesign: questions are grouped into categories a visitor would actually think in (NDIS, Billing & Medicare, Services & Access, Privacy & Rights), answers stay in plain language, and there's always a direct line to a real person if the answer isn't there.

Performance data

Results, not just a redesign

Because this was a real, live client site rather than a concept, the redesign has real before-and-after numbers behind it.

GTmetrix grade
E → A
Full grade jump on the live site.
Lighthouse performance
38% → 89%
More than double the original score.
Load time
5.6s → 2.7s
Roughly half the original load time.
A four-year partnership

Why this client stuck around

This wasn't a one-off project. Staying on as the sole design contact since 2022 meant treating every update as part of one continuous relationship rather than restarting trust each time, which shows in how willing the client has been to act on harder feedback, like the ongoing conversation about participant photo consent on the live site.

The 2026 Enablement Award now lives on the site itself, alongside community events like the Sydney Disability Connection Expo, part of treating the site as a living relationship rather than a one-time deliverable.

Interface

Screens

Beyond the core service and NDIS pages already shown above, the redesign covers the site's full breadth: group programs for kids, downloadable NDIS resources, both clinic locations, and a contact experience built around how people actually prefer to reach out.

Creative and Active Kids

A dedicated program page for the group activities Sydney Gentle Care runs for younger participants, each activity type given its own plain-language description rather than being folded into the general services list.

Resources & downloads

Official NDIS forms and guides, previously scattered or missing entirely, now live in one place with direct links to the source documents, so a participant or carer isn't stuck hunting for a PDF.

Locations

Both clinics get equal billing, with address, direct phone, email, and a one-tap booking or directions action, so the last step of the journey is as low-friction as the first.

Contact

Rather than a single generic enquiry form, the contact page splits into a directory of direct lines for General Enquiries, Admin, Accounts, and Management, alongside a structured form that asks who manages someone's NDIS plan up front, so the enquiry reaches the right person the first time.
